promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Rusting of iron and its prevention
Extraction of iron in the blast furnace

questions.q: In terms of oxygen, what is oxidation?
questions.explain: Oxidation is defined as the gain of oxygen (and reduction as the loss of oxygen).

questions.q: Using OILRIG, reduction in terms of electrons is:
questions.explain: OILRIG: Reduction Is Gain of electrons.

questions.q: In terms of electrons, oxidation is:
questions.explain: OILRIG: Oxidation Is Loss of electrons.

questions.q: In the reaction Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2, which substance is reduced?
questions.explain: Iron(III) oxide loses oxygen, so it is reduced to iron.

questions.q: In the reaction Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2, which substance is oxidised?
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide gains oxygen to become carbon dioxide, so it is oxidised.

questions.q: Which substance acts as the reducing agent that removes oxygen from the iron ore in the blast furnace?
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide reduces iron(III) oxide to iron and is itself oxidised to carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which set lists the three solid raw materials added at the top of the blast furnace?
questions.explain: Iron ore (haematite), coke and limestone are added at the top, with hot air blasted in near the bottom.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of haematite, the main ore of iron?
questions.explain: Haematite is iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3.

questions.q: Coke, added to the blast furnace, is mainly made of which element?
questions.explain: Coke is almost pure carbon and acts as both a fuel and a source of the reducing agent.

questions.q: Why is limestone added to the blast furnace?
options: To remove sandy (silica) impurities as slag
To provide the oxygen needed for combustion
To reduce the iron ore directly to iron
To lower the temperature of the furnace
questions.explain: Limestone decomposes to calcium oxide, which reacts with acidic silica impurities to form molten slag.

questions.q: Limestone used in the blast furnace is which compound?
questions.explain: Limestone is calcium carbonate, CaCO3.

questions.q: Which equation correctly shows the thermal decomposition of limestone in the furnace?
questions.explain: The heat decomposes calcium carbonate into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Calcium oxide reacts with silica (SiO2) impurities in the furnace. What is the product, known as slag?
questions.explain: CaO + SiO2 -> CaSiO3, the molten slag that floats on top of the iron.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the reaction C + O2 -> CO2 at the base of the furnace?
options: It is exothermic and supplies the heat for the process
It reduces the iron ore to iron
It cools the incoming iron ore
questions.explain: Burning coke in the hot air blast is strongly exothermic and provides the high temperatures needed.

questions.q: Which equation shows how carbon monoxide is produced in the furnace?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide rises and reacts with more hot coke to form carbon monoxide, the reducing agent.

questions.q: Chemically, what is rust?
questions.explain: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water.

questions.q: Which two substances must both be present for iron to rust?
questions.explain: Rusting requires both water and oxygen (from the air); removing either prevents it.

questions.q: An iron nail is placed in a test tube of boiled water covered with a layer of oil. After several days, what is observed and why?
options: No rust, because the oil layer keeps oxygen out
Heavy rust, because boiling adds oxygen
No rust, because boiling removes all the water
Rust only at the water surface, because of extra acid
questions.explain: Boiling removes dissolved oxygen and the oil stops air redissolving, so with no oxygen the nail cannot rust.

questions.q: What does galvanising an iron object involve?
options: Coating it with a layer of zinc
Coating it with a layer of tin
Painting it with a plastic layer
questions.explain: Galvanising coats iron with zinc, which acts as both a barrier and sacrificial protection.

questions.q: Blocks of magnesium are bolted to the steel hull of a ship. How does this prevent rusting?
options: Magnesium is more reactive and corrodes instead of the iron (sacrificial protection)
Magnesium forms a waterproof paint layer
Magnesium removes the oxygen from the seawater chemically
Magnesium makes the iron less reactive by coating it with tin
questions.explain: Being more reactive, magnesium is oxidised in preference to the iron, protecting it sacrificially.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Chemistry (2017) specification; Redox, Rusting & Iron
